rationale: unit:shared.well_formed matches Allocated, Live, References, Owners, Compatible and WellFormed. Allocated is object-key membership; Live starts at any initialized variable and follows initialized fields independent of reference mode. Owners preserves occurrences across variables and all fields, so Pairwise Compatible is about distinct positions, including equal shared reference values. For equal targets Compatible requires both modes shared, exactly excluding a unique occurrence with any second owner. referencesComplete is a biconditional: every stored target is allocated and every allocated object has at least one owning occurrence. objectKeys/variableKeys give distinct table keys; shapes fixes class membership, declaration field order and field-name distinctness; bounds and older require counter-bounded identities and strictly decreasing object IDs along fields. These match each prose condition. A finite field cycle would contradict strict decreasing natural identities, so the explanation of rootless cycles is justified by this invariant rather than by a mistaken single-owner assumption. The revised final paragraph correctly distinguishes a unique stored reference, which must be the sole incoming owning occurrence, from unique path access, which also requires every preceding reference to be unique. The stated local condition is a sufficient representation invariant, not asserted to be equivalent to the user's path-level requirement by itself.
